purpose: Replay alpha.11 across all enabled rules and the full normalized report.
applicability: Enabled rules are not all applicable. Framework detection, finding/UNKNOWN rule IDs and declared limitations describe the checked envelope.

findings.title: Session cookie protection is explicitly disabled

evidence.message: secure is explicitly false on an authentication or session cookie.

findings.securityInvariant: Authentication session cookies must be protected from cleartext transport and client-side script access.
findings.attackPrerequisite: An attacker can observe an insecure transport path or execute script in the cookie's origin.
findings.impact: A stolen session token can allow account impersonation until the session is revoked or expires.
findings.remediation: Set Secure and HttpOnly for authentication cookies, verify SameSite and scope, and test the deployed HTTPS path.

findings.title: Ambiently authenticated state-changing route lacks a proven anti-CSRF control

evidence.message: Proven POST /command-injection-vulnerable relies on ambient browser credentials without a supported route-bound anti-CSRF control.

findings.attackPrerequisite: A victim browser holds an ambient application credential and can be induced to send a cross-site request accepted by the state-changing route.
findings.impact: An attacker can cause unauthorized state changes using the victim's automatically attached credentials.
findings.remediation: Bind a framework-supported anti-CSRF token or exact request-origin control to the route architecture; do not rely on method choice or SameSite alone without reviewing browser semantics.

source.label: Supported Express session/cookie authentication supplies an ambient browser credential

propagationPath.label: Security IR binds ambient authentication to POST /command-injection-vulnerable

proof.conclusion: The supported state-changing route is reachable with ambient credentials and no supported request-origin control is bound to it.
analysisLimitations: CSRF proof is bounded to literal Express routes, repository-local ESM middleware/handler resolution, supported ambient credential evidence, and explicit route-bound controls.

findings.title: Untrusted input controls shell syntax

evidence.message: Proven untrusted request data controls a shell command string or shell-enabled process invocation.

findings.attackPrerequisite: An attacker can control the proven request value supplied to shell parsing.
findings.impact: Injected shell syntax can execute commands with the application's operating-system privileges.
findings.remediation: Remove shell interpretation and invoke an explicitly chosen executable with a validated argument array; review argument-level injection semantics separately.

proof.conclusion: UNTRUSTED_INPUT_MUST_NOT_CONTROL_SHELL_SYNTAX is violated by a complete, reachable source-to-sink path.
analysisLimitations: The proof is bounded to statically resolved repository-local propagation and the documented sink model.

findings.title: Untrusted input reaches a raw browser rendering context

evidence.message: Proven untrusted input reaches a supported RAW_HTML browser rendering sink without a context-appropriate control.

findings.attackPrerequisite: An attacker can control the proven input and cause the supported response or DOM rendering path to execute in a victim browser.
findings.impact: Attacker-controlled browser-interpreted content can execute script in the application's origin and act with the victim's privileges.
findings.remediation: Use framework autoescaping or context-specific output encoding; where trusted rich HTML is required, use a reviewed HTML sanitizer and constrain URL and script contexts separately.

proof.conclusion: UNTRUSTED_BROWSER_CONTENT_MUST_NOT_REACH_RAW_RENDERING_WITHOUT_A_CONTEXT_APPROPRIATE_CONTROL is violated by a complete, reachable source-to-sink path.
analysisLimitations: The proof is bounded to statically resolved repository-local propagation and the documented sink model.

findings.title: Untrusted input controls a server-side request destination

evidence.message: Proven untrusted request data controls the destination of a recognized server-side HTTP request without an enforced destination policy.

findings.attackPrerequisite: An attacker can control the proven destination component of a server-side request.
findings.impact: The server may access internal services, cloud metadata, loopback listeners, or attacker-selected destinations using its network position.
findings.remediation: Enforce an organization-defined normalized destination policy covering scheme and hostname, and review port, DNS resolution, redirect, and proxy behavior.

proof.conclusion: UNTRUSTED_NETWORK_DESTINATION_MUST_NOT_CONTROL_SERVER_SIDE_REQUEST_TARGET_WITHOUT_ENFORCED_POLICY is violated by a complete, reachable source-to-sink path.
analysisLimitations: The proof is bounded to statically resolved repository-local propagation and the documented sink model.

findings.title: Untrusted input controls SQL statement structure

evidence.message: Proven untrusted request data controls SQL statement structure at a recognized database sink without separate parameterization.

findings.attackPrerequisite: An attacker can control the proven request value reaching the database call.
findings.impact: Injected SQL structure can disclose, modify, or delete data and may bypass application authorization.
findings.remediation: Use the database library's parameterized query interface and separately constrain any dynamic identifiers to an explicit application-defined allowlist.

engineCompleteness.details: Repository traversal completed within configured bounds.
All supported source files parsed successfully.

limitations: Only explicit, evidence-backed supported patterns are evaluated; absence of findings is not a security guarantee.
Working-tree state was obtained with a five-second/one-MiB no-lock Git status probe; repository hooks/fsmonitor and submodule inspection were disabled.
Python analysis validates syntax but phase-one Python rules use exact configuration/call patterns rather than semantic name resolution.
No repository code, lifecycle script, hook, build, test, container, or network operation was executed.
Git history was not analyzed; use cydetix secrets . --history.
Dependency advisories were NOT_CHECKED_OFFLINE; this is not a zero-vulnerability result.
Generated code, runtime configuration, and dependency function reachability were not analyzed.
Phase two projects statically resolved Express routes, identity provenance, Prisma resources, and authorization/tenant proof states.
Authentication Graph v2 projects adapter-guaranteed lifecycle operations, validation boundaries, trust transitions, revocation events, and invariant results.
Generated routes, dynamic middleware composition, unsupported ORM behavior, and runtime policy remain UNKNOWN.
The absence of a graph edge is not evidence that a security control is absent.
Cross-file call resolution is limited to repository-local relative ESM imports and statically named direct or namespace calls.
CommonJS require, tsconfig path aliases, package exports, re-exports, dependency injection, decorators, computed properties, and runtime dispatch remain UNKNOWN.
Express routes require literal paths and statically named handlers; inline and dynamically composed handlers remain UNKNOWN.
Authenticated Express identity is trusted only when a statically bound middleware proves credential verification and authenticated-context assignment.
Identity propagation follows positional arguments across resolved calls only; aliases, mutation, closures, destructuring, and returned values remain UNKNOWN.
Prisma analysis supports direct prisma.<model> operations with flat literal where selectors; nested, spread, relational, raw, and dynamically built queries remain UNKNOWN.
JavaScript/TypeScript propagation is bounded to direct assignments, aliases, object properties, templates, concatenation, resolved same-file calls, arguments, and returns.
Python propagation is bounded to parsed decorated routes and local assignments; cross-function and cross-file Python propagation is unsupported.
Unknown custom sanitizers and unresolved dynamic transformations produce UNKNOWN instead of an actionable finding.
No target code, package script, hook, framework CLI, test, build, or arbitrary interpreter was executed.
Phase 3 authentication proofs cover explicit TypeScript/JavaScript Express, express-session, Prisma authentication records, jsonwebtoken, jose, and oauth4webapi evidence only.
Library behavior is trusted only for the exact supported API surface; version-hidden or unsupported behavior remains UNKNOWN.
Application names alone never establish an authentication operation; adapters require protocol APIs, persistence operations, or resolved lifecycle evidence.
OAuth 2.1 remains an Internet-Draft and is not used as normative detector guidance.
